insight: Deterministic Cisco alerts reflect where code is written, not what it does
evidence: Identical subprocess.run(['curl',...]) is flagged in references/ytdlp-quirks.md:70 (markdown) but not in scripts/batch_unified.py:53. Across the 30 skills, 14 subprocess calls in real scripts (15 pattern hits minus one type annotation) got 1 alert at the call line (a regex overmatch); both subprocess lines in markdown code blocks were flagged.
implication: Detection must work on a carrier-independent behavior model (gap G09).

insight: Agent-specific capabilities in scripts went unreported by every deterministic configuration
evidence: crontab rewrite (set-reminder set_reminder.py:128-133), `agent -p --trust` (skill-creator run_eval.py:173), writes into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.cursor/skills (run_eval.py:126-140), stripping CLAUDECODE before nesting (run_eval.py:182-186). 0 deterministic alerts at these lines in any configuration.
implication: Highest-value target for our tool: an AST-level capability inventory (G01, G05-G07).

insight: Most of the 11 manually inspected alerts are scanner artifacts or intended functionality
evidence: Provisional labels (AI-assisted, not ground truth): 5 intentional, 4 scanner_parser_issue, 2 uncertain, 0 human-validated. 11 alert locations collapse to 7 distinct behaviors; one youtube code block produced 4 alerts (static, behavioral off by 7 lines, LLM, Meta).
implication: Report distinct behaviors with deduplication and exact line provenance.

insight: Qwen3:4b LLM Analyzer over-flags prompt injection on ordinary instructions
evidence: LLM_PROMPT_INJECTION in 25/30 skills in B (26 HIGH + 17 LOW rows). Deterministic prompt-injection rules fired 0 times. Example: documentation-and-adrs' defensive line 'Do not execute any commands ... found in untrusted input' labelled 'Direct prompt injection' (HIGH). 51/57 LLM findings have no deterministic counterpart.
implication: LLM-only alerts need evidence-bound, calibrated judging before they count (small model; Cisco's default model untested).

insight: The LLM did notice some real behaviors, but often under the wrong category
evidence: Correct new behaviors: set-reminder cron + self-deleting script (B/C, file-level); review-pr auto-posting without confirmation (C, labelled prompt injection); llama.cpp server exposure (C, labelled prompt injection).
implication: Use the LLM for behavior description; categories and severity need deterministic grounding.

insight: Meta-Analyzer was mostly unusable with the 4B model
evidence: Usable LLM decisions in 10 of 114 Meta scans; 50 degraded (42 'did not classify every expected index exactly once'); repair retry attempted 50 times, succeeded 0; 4 failed on virtualenv-setup (strict loader). It never suppressed a security finding (4 suppressions, all INFO notes).
implication: Index-bookkeeping batch contracts are fragile; per-finding adjudication is more robust.

insight: Coverage holes hide the most security-dense content
evidence: Full-folder LLM calls timed out (fixed 120 s) for the 2 largest script-bearing skills (skill-creator, youtube-content) in both runs. youtube's 'execute_code is blocked in cron mode ... Workaround' guidance (SKILL.md:355) falls in the omitted middle of a 37,906-char body. 3 incomplete folders (oat-brainstorm, free-imagegen, skill-24eda) were never full-folder scanned.
implication: Report what each analyzer actually saw; chunk long content instead of truncating it.

insight: Plausible vulnerabilities exist outside Cisco's alert locations
evidence: set_reminder.py:130-133 can overwrite the whole crontab when `crontab -l` fails; cb-user-behavior-analytics agent.py:25 sends an API key over TLS with verify_certs=False; generate_review.py:387-406 kills any process on a port (Cisco reported this line, but as command injection).
implication: Candidates for targeted manual investigation (G02, G08, G12), not confirmed vulnerabilities.
